summary:
LunarPath AI is an interactive educational web tool for planning simulated missions to the lunar South Pole. Users choose candidate sites from the Artemis III regions and a date, and the tool shows when and where there is sunlight and a direct line of sight to Earth.

It addresses the challenge by combining three NASA resources. JPL Horizons provides the real positions of the Sun and Earth as seen from the Moon. LOLA terrain data from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) shows which mountains and crater rims block the horizon. Moon Trek maps place each site in context. From this data, the tool calculates continuous windows of illumination and communication, compares sites with an explainable ranking, displays an illumination calendar, and estimates battery energy, with 2D and 3D visualizations.

This matters because at the South Pole the Sun and Earth barely rise above the horizon, so a small ridge can decide whether a robot has power or contact. Work that normally requires specialized tools becomes understandable for students and the public, while the tool stays clear about its limits: it does not certify landing safety or radio links.
details:
4. Core Page Functionalities

4.1 Home Screen & Orbital Transition

  • Outreach Landing (EducationView): Introduces the platform over a rotating 3D Moon and breaks down mission planning into three intuitive steps (01 / Time: Pick a date, 02 / Energy: Find the light, 03 / Communication: Look back home).
  • Orbital Loading (OrbitalLoading): Animated orbital transition screen when entering the explorer or switching views.

4.2 Interactive 3D Solar System Viewer (Sun – Earth – Moon)

  • Bottom-bar focus presets: Smooth camera transitions between Vista general (Sun), Tierra (Earth), Luna (Moon), and Tierra + Luna, plus Detener / Reanudar to pause or resume orbital motion and rotation.
  • Free 3D navigation: Mouse orbit/pan (OrbitControls with screen-space panning) and keyboard flight controls (W/A/S/D, Arrow keys, Q/E, Space/Ctrl, and Shift boost).
  • Accurate 3D depth occlusion: Configured with a standard depth buffer (logarithmicDepthBuffer: false) so Earth and the Moon are properly occluded when passing behind the Sun.

4.3 Lunar Explorer (Main Console)

  • Georeferenced polar map (IAU2000::30120): Switches between LROC imagery and LOLA elevation relief, supports multi-level zoom into local NAC/LOLA tiles, and allows custom site selection by clicking the map or entering latitude/longitude.
  • 360° Horizon & visibility: Plots the real terrain horizon across all 360 azimuths alongside hourly Sun and Earth trajectories, angular clearance, and dominant terrain obstacles.
  • Scientific uncertainty: Propagates spatial perturbations across 4 neighboring points (±240 m) and LOLA vertical DEM error (±3σ).
  • Power & communications simulation: Models solar generation, battery state of charge (presets: VIPER-class Polar Rover, Medium CLPS Lander, Artemis Solar Tower / Hab), and direct Earth communication windows.
  • 3D terrain & slope: Renders local 3D elevation meshes and computes regional terrain slope.

4.4 Illumination Calendar (e.g., Mons Mouton)

  • Color-coded monthly view: Evaluates every day of the month by the percentage of hours the solar disk stays above the real terrain horizon:
    • Green (Favorable): 70% or more sunlight.
    • Yellow (Almost favorable): between 30% and 70%.
    • Red (Near zero): more than 0% and less than 30%.
    • Uncolored (No sunlight): 0%.
  • Date-synchronized 3D Moon: Selecting any day (for example, November 23, 2026 at Mons Mouton) illuminates the 3D Moon at the exact solar elevation and azimuth of that day's peak moment, highlighting the site with a blue marker.

4.5 Guided Planning, Comparison, Ranking & AI Copilot

  • Guided Planning (MissionPlanningView), Results (MissionResultsView), and Detail (MissionDetailView): Step-by-step wizard to select date, duration, priority (Light, Earth, or Balanced), and compare two South Pole sites over a 7-day window.
  • Compare & Ranking: Weighted multi-site scoring and Mission Delta sensitivity analysis (impact of launch delays or landing-site shifts).
  • Mission Copilot: Answers natural-language questions grounded strictly in computed metrics and parses textual requirements into operational constraints.
  • CSV Export & Light/Dark Theme: Exports complete scenario reports with scientific metadata and supports light/dark theme switching across the console.
